base_member_text: [L43-L50] (MED/collective-input-error) Root reads interactive input without EOF or conversion-error handling before broadcasting, so input failure can terminate root while peers wait in the collective.
audit_member_text: [L46-L50] (MED/input-error-handling) The root's formatted input has no IOSTAT or end/error branch, so EOF or malformed input terminates that process while other ranks can remain waiting in MPI_BCAST.

adversarial.rationale: Root performs the formatted i10 read before the broadcast, with no IOSTAT, END or ERR branch; the n<=0 exit check happens only after successful input and broadcast. An MPI launcher may subsequently tear down the job, but the example has no collective handling of root EOF/conversion failure and peers can be left waiting until that cleanup.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L59-L62] (LOW/integer-overflow) Unbounded positive input permits a DO-loop terminal increment beyond the default-integer range for sufficiently large n.
audit_member_text: [L59-L62] (MED/integer-overflow) An interval count near the default integer limit can overflow the DO iteration count or final induction-variable increment.

adversarial.rationale: The overflow possibility survives the n<=0 guard: i10 accepts 2147483647 and, with one process, the final default-integer induction value would be 2147483648. Reduce severity to LOW because this is an extreme-input portability defect in an interactive demonstration, with actual termination/overflow behavior depending on how the compiler implements or eliminates the DO control variable.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check
